chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who says, “I seek forgiveness of Allah,” one hundred times every day, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will forgive him seven hundred sins, and there is no good in a servant who sins every day, seven hundred times.'
ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of reciting Istighfar one hundred times a day according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the specific practice of reciting *Astaghfirullah* one hundred times daily to the expiation of seven hundred sins, illustrating the immense mercy of Allah in balancing human frailty. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on consistent, daily repentance as a means to maintain spiritual purity, while also serving as a diagnostic tool: a servant who accumulates such a high volume of daily sins is deemed lacking in true spiritual goodness (*la khayra fi 'abd*).

en.hubeali: Mhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ammar Bin Marwan who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who says, ‘I seek Forgiveness of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, one hundred times during every day, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Forgive seven hundred sins for him, and there is no good in a servant who sins during every day, seven hundred times’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ‘Ammar ibn Marwan who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘If one says, “I plead for forgiveness before Allah” one hundred times every day, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will forgive his seven hundred sins, but there is nothing good in a servant (of Allah) who commits seven hundred sins a day.’”
